The closest recurrent precedent is [MTAM (CIKM 2020)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598): temporal gates modify recurrent state transitions and information filtering; a time-aware GRU captures short-term intent, with historical memory supplying longer-term preferences. [LSARN (2023 preprint)](https://ssrn.com/abstract=4336514) likewise introduces two time gates inside a time-GRU. More recent [TLSTSRec (online 2024; volume 2025)](https://doi.org/10.3233/IDA-240051) combines temporal information with adaptive long-/short-term fusion, but uses a Transformer. These findings support learned temporal conditioning as an established mechanism; they do not establish improvements under the specified Amazon HR@10 protocol.

A focused experiment, inferred from these mechanisms: retain GRU4Rec and jointly train one small gate conditioned on item features and log-transformed elapsed time, modulating hidden-state retention before the GRU update. Initialize near full retention to limit disruption of the corrected baseline. Use only observed historical inter-event gaps available consistently during training and inference; never use the unknown next-event timestamp. Compare against the corrected GRU using fixed seeds, splits and macro validation HR@10, with one checkpoint per category. Preserve padding masks, final-nonpadding readout, diagnostic interfaces and identical predictor serialization. Feature-wise gating is also motivated by [TLSRec (CIKM 2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04760), which argues that a single scalar can be too coarse for balancing persistent and transient interests; its attention backbone need not be adopted.
